result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A and B both explain the rendering and pixel-density causes well, are honest that some differences can't be removed, and say heavier weights are the main fix. A wins on rubric item 2 because it gives a concrete size bump (16px body, 300→400) where B suggests only a 12px minimum and advises changing the face before raising size. A is more jargon-heavy (Core Text, FreeType, stem darkening) and ends with an odd remark about the working directory, while B adds a useful point about the designer possibly using a locally installed font but wrongly says Windows keeps shapes closer to their true outline. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly blame rendering differences rather than CSS, and both recommend heavier weights. B is slightly better: it describes Windows grid-fitting more accurately, adds useful advice on contrast and a 16px body size, gives an honest reality check, and notes that DevTools emulation can't reproduce how each platform renders text. A is a little easier for a non-specialist to read and usefully mentions the designer's locally installed font, but its Windows explanation is muddled and its 12px minimum is weak advice. B's closing remark about the working directory is out of place.
